page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The server is configured with 1344.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on external premium storage options.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, alongside strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the average range, including uncached large-block read and write speeds. LLM inference benchmarks show strong text generation speeds for small models, while larger models perform at average rates.

From a resource density perspective, the FX64-16ms_v2 offers high memory capacity relative to its vCPU count, making it a specialized option for memory-bound workloads. However, the absence of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which may introduce latency and additional configuration requirements. The high-frequency Intel Xeon processor provides strong single-threaded performance, but the 16 vCPU limit may constrain highly parallelized multi-threaded tasks.

This server configuration is suited for memory-intensive applications that require high single-core performance but do not demand massive parallelization. Appropriate workloads include large in-memory databases, memory-bound enterprise applications, single-threaded data processing pipelines, and text-processing applications.
